title: OData service
description: Any OData service, v2 or v4: its entity sets become tables, with their keys, links and descriptions from its $metadata.

fields.name: url
fields.label: Service URL
fields.help: The service's address. Any address from it works too — its $metadata, or an entity set's: the service is found from it.

fields.name: auth
fields.label: Sign-in
fields.help: none: an open service. basic: a user and a password. api-key: a key sent in a header. oauth-client: an OAuth client (client credentials).

fields.name: apiKeyHeader
fields.label: Header for the key
fields.help: The name of the header the key is sent in, as the service's documentation names it.

fields.name: tokenUrl
fields.label: Token URL
fields.help: Where the client gets its access token.

fields.name: scope
fields.label: Scope
fields.help: Only if the token URL asks for one (for Microsoft: the resource followed by /.default).

fields.name: entitySets
fields.label: Entity sets
fields.help: Which entity sets to read, separated by commas or one per line; every one of the service when empty.

setup.title: Where the service is
setup.say: Paste the service's address, as the engine will reach it — its root (often ending in .svc/ or /odata/), or any address from it: its $metadata, or one of its entity sets. The service is found from it.

setup.title: Sign in, to read
setup.say:
How the service lets the engine in. Superatom only reads: give it an account, key or client that may read and nothing more, where the service lets you choose.

basic — a user and its password. api-key — the key, and the header it goes in (APIKey unless the service's documentation names another). oauth-client — a client registered with the service's sign-in provider: its token URL, client ID and secret, and the scope it asks for, if any.

The check reads the service's $metadata and one row.

fix.say: The token URL refused the client. Check the client ID and secret (a secret is often shown only once, when it is made), and the scope.

fix.when: did not answer with an OData service|not an OData service
fix.say: Something answers at that address, but it is not an OData service. Paste the service's own address — the one whose $metadata describes its entity sets.
The service sent a sign-in web page instead of data: it wants a sign-in the engine did not give. Choose how it signs in (basic, api-key or oauth-client) and give the credentials.

setup.title: What to read
setup.say: Leave it empty to read every entity set of the service, or name the ones to read (Customers, Orders). The check lists what it will read.

fix.say: One of the names is not an entity set of this service. Names are case-sensitive: copy them from the list shown.
